citation: Farenhorst, R. and de Boer, R.C.: Architectural Knowledge Management: Supporting Architects and Auditors, PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, defended 5 Oct 2009 (SIKS Dissertation Series No. 2009-32). A single shared thesis text defended jointly by both authors the same day; the VU Research Portal catalogs it under de Boer's name alone, which the inventory row's citation follows.
problem_addressed: Architectural knowledge (design decisions, rationale, considered alternatives) is mostly tacit, undocumented and lost after the fact -- 'architectural knowledge vaporization' -- causing expensive evolution, poor stakeholder communication and lost reuse; the thesis asks what architectural knowledge is and how to manage/share it to support architects and auditors.
state_model: No formal ontological/epistemic/lifecycle state triple. Proposes a unifying 'core model of architectural knowledge' (Ch.4) synthesizing prior decision-centric models into concepts (decision, alternative, argument/rationale, issue, stakeholder) and their relations, but as an informal conceptual/UML-style model, not an executable state abstraction.
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no typed S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 transition semantics; decisions are recorded with status and rationale but the core model does not define an append-only transition log or transition typing scheme.
provenance_model: Informal only: decisions are attributed to architects/stakeholders and carry rationale and considered alternatives, but there is no structured provenance schema analogous to actor+authority+evidence+method+lineage+delegation; provenance is narrative, captured via tool fields and interviews/action research, not a queryable graph.
actor_model: Architects and auditors as the two supported roles; social network analysis (Ch.3.5.3) maps communities in which architectural knowledge circulates, and the GRIFFIN tool targets collaborative multi-stakeholder knowledge sharing -- a real actor/community topology, but oriented at who talks to whom, not at authority-weighted epistemic arbitration.
temporal_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- no bitemporal or explicit temporal-versioning model was found in the chapters read (Ch.1-2, part of Ch.3); GRIFFIN tool chapters (Part II/III) were not reached in this pass and might refine this.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- the thesis addresses knowledge capture and sharing, not conflicting-evidence arbitration or trust scoring between competing claims.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no independence-aware corroboration mechanism; not addressed.
memory_model: The GRIFFIN collaborative platform functions as a shared repository/community memory for architectural knowledge artifacts (decisions, rationale, patterns); positioned as a knowledge-management tool rather than a versioned or queryable memory architecture.
retrieval_context_model: Community/repository-based retrieval and sharing (GRIFFIN), plus quality-criteria elicitation via the repertory grid technique for selecting relevant architectural knowledge; not a topology-aware, lineage/dissent-weighted context-selection mechanism.
decision_representation: Central and strongest overlap: decisions are first-class objects carrying rationale and considered alternatives, unifying earlier decision-centric models (Kruchten, Bosch, Tyree & Akerman) into one 'core model' -- structurally close to D-System's decision node, at a 2009 pre-formal, human-authored maturity level.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- out of scope; the thesis treats requirements as an input constraining decisions, not as a derived/traceable output of decisions.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no software-execution or agent-session model.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- architectural knowledge is linked to architecture documentation and decisions, not to source code or build artifacts, in the chapters read.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; this is a pre-DevOps-era (2009) knowledge-management thesis with no runtime-telemetry feedback loop.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: Partial: the action-research cycle with GRIFFIN's industrial partners (design theory -> experimentation -> mismatch identification -> refinement) is itself a feedback loop for improving the *research's* core model, and auditors are meant to feed compliance findings back to architects, but this is a research/organizational process, not an automated runtime-to-knowledge mechanism.
forward_traceability: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS in the chapters read (Ch.1-2, part of Ch.3); auditor-support chapters (Part III, not reached this pass) may define decision-to-compliance traceability more concretely.
backward_traceability: Decision rationale and considered alternatives provide a backward trace from a decision to why it was made, matching D-System's H9 backward direction conceptually, but only as narrative documentation, not a queryable graph edge.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no epistemic blast-radius / change-impact propagation mechanism found in the chapters read.
human_agent_scope: Human-only (architects, auditors); 2009, pre-agentic. No AI/agent actor is modeled.
implementation_availability: Academic prototype only: the GRIFFIN collaborative platform and repertory-grid quality-criteria tooling were research artifacts of the GRIFFIN project (2005-2009); no evidence found in this pass that GRIFFIN is a maintained or publicly available system today.
evaluation_method: Systematic literature review (state of the art) + social network analysis of AK communities + action research with four industrial partners (Astron Foundation, DNV-CIBIT, Getronics PinkRoccade, Logica) over the GRIFFIN project's lifetime.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: Names and analyzes 'architectural knowledge vaporization' -- the loss of undocumented decision rationale -- as its central problem, 15+ years before D-System's own conception, and proposes decisions-plus-rationale-plus-alternatives as first-class knowledge objects, directly anticipating the motivating premise behind D-System's H7 and H9.
strongest_difference: No formal state/transition/provenance data model, no typed append-only transition log, no agentic actors, and no linkage beyond architecture decisions into requirements, specifications, code, tests, deployment or runtime evidence -- the thesis is confined to the Reasoning/Decision stage of D-System's proposed lifecycle and relies on qualitative/social research methods and a bespoke collaborative tool rather than a structured graph or database architecture.
derivative_ancestor: jansen-bosch-architecture-as-decisions-wicsa-2005 (this batch); tradition traces further back to Kruchten, P., Architectural Blueprints -- The 4+1 View Model of Software Architecture, IEEE Software, 1995, and Perry, D.E. & Wolf, A.L., Foundations for the Study of Software Architecture, ACM SIGSOFT SEN 17(4), 1992 (Software Architecture = {Elements, Form, Rationale}) -- the origin of rationale as a first-class architecture element that both the de Boer/Farenhorst core model and the Jansen & Bosch decision view inherit.
evidence_locator: Title/author/defense pages (unnumbered front matter, pp.i-xvii, esp. Acknowledgments p.xvii: 'The fact that Rik and I eventually wrote a single thesis together...'); Ch.1 Introduction pp.1-3 (software architecture background, Perry & Wolf 1992 quoted p.3: 'Software Architecture = {Elements, Form, Rationale}'); Ch.2 pp.9-11 (research questions RQ-I.1/I.2/I.3, methodology, outline of Part I noting Ch.4's unifying decision-centric core model); Table of Contents p.vii (Ch.3.2 'What is Architectural Knowledge', Ch.3.4 'Philosophies of AKM', Ch.3.5.3 'Social network analysis').
verbatim_notes: p.xvii: 'The fact that Rik and I eventually wrote a single thesis together is in my opinion indicative for the collegiality within our team.' p.3 (quoting Perry & Wolf 1992): 'Software Architecture = { Elements, Form, Rationale }... rationale as the motivation for the architectural choices made.' p.9: 'RQ-I.1 What is architectural knowledge? RQ-I.2 How can architectural knowledge be managed? RQ-I.3 What are typical challenges to architectural knowledge management in practice?'

citation: Kasibatla, S.R., Rothkopf, R., Peleg, H., Pierce, B.C., Lerner, S., Goldstein, H., Polikarpova, N.: Decision-Oriented Programming with Aporia, arXiv preprint, submitted 6 Apr 2026 (UC San Diego, Technion, U Penn, Cornell, U Buffalo).
problem_addressed: AI coding agents let developers express intent abstractly, but developers cede decision-making authority to the agent and lose visibility into the design choices it makes silently, eroding their mental model of their own codebase ('cognitive debt'); the paper proposes decision-oriented programming (DOP) to keep programmers in the loop on the decisions an agent makes on their behalf.
state_model: A Decision is the first-class state object: a persistent, editable record in the Decision Bank holding the elicited question, the programmer's yes/no answer plus optional free-text comment, and links to relevant code. No separate ontological/epistemic/lifecycle classification triple; a decision is a flat record, not a typed multi-dimensional state.
transition_model: Decisions are edited or revoked in place ('users can edit or revoke' a Decision Bank entry) rather than appended as a new typed transition preserving the prior value; no evidence in the sections read of a retained history of a decision's prior answers, so this is closer to mutable state than D-System's append-only S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 transition log.
provenance_model: Each decision carries the agent's rationale for the question/options (shown in the Question Detail View) and a pointer to the relevant code passage that motivated it, but there is no actor/authority/evidence/method/lineage/delegation schema; provenance is limited to agent-generated rationale text plus a code reference, not a structured multi-actor provenance graph.
actor_model: Two actors only: the programmer and a single coding agent, in a tight elicit/decide/implement/validate loop (Fig.1); no multi-agent, multi-stakeholder or authority-weighted actor model.
temporal_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- no explicit temporal/versioning model described in the sections read (pp.1-4); the Decision Bank's edit/revoke behavior implies at most current-value semantics, not a bitemporal record.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- single-agent, single-user tool; no conflicting-claim arbitration or trust weighting.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no multi-source corroboration concept.
memory_model: The Decision Bank itself is the memory model: a persistent, structured, user-visible, per-project record of design decisions, distinct from the coding agent's own conversational or embedding-based memory.
retrieval_context_model: Decisions are surfaced contextually as Question Bubbles inline in the file being edited, with a Detail View showing rationale and clickable references to relevant code; this is intent-scoped (per active goal/file) retrieval, not a topology-aware retrieval over lineage, dissent or authority.
decision_representation: Central and closely matching: decisions are explicit, structured, first-class, persistent, editable objects that are the 'shared medium through which programmer and agent negotiate the design' (DG1) -- directly on D-System's decision-node concept, with the added twist that the agent (not just the human) proactively initiates each decision.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE in the mechanism read: the user states a free-text 'Goal' at the top of the sidebar, and questions/decisions are generated relevant to that goal, but no distinct, persisted requirement artifact separate from the goal string and the Decision Bank entries was described.
specification_representation: Each decision is formally encoded as an executable test suite (DG3) -- the test suite functions as an executable specification of that one decision, giving 'an unambiguous interpretation of their decisions.' This is a concrete, code-adjacent specification representation, narrower than D-System's general specification stage but mechanistically real.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no explicit phase/plan artifact; the workflow is goal -> elicit questions -> accumulate decisions -> 'Implement plan' action, which is a single interaction loop rather than a multi-step plan structure.
execution_unit_session_model: The goal-scoped elicit/decide/implement/validate loop (Fig.1) is the closest analog to an execution unit: bounded by one stated Goal, not by an explicit phase/session object with its own lifecycle.
artifact_code_linkage: Direct and concrete: each Decision Bank entry links to the relevant code passage, and the 'Implement plan' action prompts the agent to modify the codebase to satisfy all decisions -- a real, working decision-to-code linkage, DG3's core claim.
test_verification_linkage: Direct and concrete: every decision generates its own executable test suite, and Aporia 'automatically runs all its generated tests to validate the implementation against the user's decisions' -- the strongest single mechanism match against D-System's H9 verification-linkage claim found in this batch.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; the tool operates entirely within the local VS Code / codebase editing loop.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no production runtime telemetry feedback loop.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE beyond the single edit/revoke loop -- a programmer can revise an existing decision at any time, which re-runs validation, but this updates the Decision Bank's current state rather than feeding a separate persistent knowledge structure.
forward_traceability: Decision -> test suite -> implemented code is explicit and automated (DG3), covering roughly the Decision -> Specification -> Execution -> Artifact -> Verification span of D-System's proposed lifecycle in one tight loop.
backward_traceability: The Question Detail View lets the programmer trace from a piece of code/behavior back to the decision and the agent's stated rationale for it -- a working, UI-surfaced backward trace matching D-System's H9 backward direction at the Decision/Artifact boundary specifically (not from Artifact all the way back to Idea/Evidence).
change_impact_mechanism: Partial: revoking or editing a decision triggers re-validation against its test suite, which is a narrow, single-decision form of change-impact propagation, not a graph-wide epistemic blast-radius analysis across dependent decisions, requirements or other artifacts.
human_agent_scope: Explicitly human-agent collaborative: a single programmer and a single AI coding agent, published in 2026, squarely in-scope for D-System's agentic framing (unlike de Boer/Farenhorst 2009 or Jansen & Bosch 2005 in this same batch).
implementation_availability: Working research prototype ('Aporia'): a VS Code extension built as a 'design probe,' evaluated in a 14-participant within-subjects user study against Claude Code as baseline; not established as a maintained public open-source release in the sections read (no repository URL found in pp.1-4).
evaluation_method: Within-subjects user study, N=14 programmers, adding features to an existing codebase using either Aporia or a baseline coding agent (Claude Code); measured engagement, scaffolding of design/validation, and mental-model-to-code mismatch rate (79% lower / 5x less likely with Aporia).
strongest_dsystem_overlap: The single strongest collision in this batch: an agentic system built in 2026 around exactly D-System's H7 (decisions as persistent, structured, code-traceable objects), H9 (bidirectional decision<->code traceability via executable test suites) and, more weakly, H8 (a goal-scoped elicit/decide/implement/validate loop as an implicit context boundary) -- as an explicit, self-described application of the decades-old QOC design-rationale tradition to agentic coding.
strongest_difference: No append-only transition history (decisions are edited/revoked in place, so H2's preserved-reasoning-history claim is not met), no multi-actor provenance/authority/conflict model (H3/H4 untouched), no requirement/plan/deployment/runtime stages, and no knowledge-construction system at all upstream of the Decision Bank -- Aporia is a tight, single-agent, single-goal decision<->code loop, not an end-to-end knowledge-to-runtime architecture.
derivative_ancestor: maclean-young-bellotti-moran-qoc-design-space-analysis-1991 (already inventoried) -- the paper states directly (Sec.2, 'Design rationales'): 'Aporia elicits decisions with questions as an application of QOC,' making this a 2026 agentic-coding instantiation of a 1991 design-rationale notation rather than an independent invention of question-elicited decision capture.
evidence_locator: Title page and Fig.1 (p.1, DOP interaction loop diagram); Abstract (p.1); Sec.1 Introduction, DG1-DG3 and Aporia's three tracked capabilities (p.2); Sec.2 Related Work, 'Design rationales' subsection citing QOC and comparing to Pail [57] (p.3); Sec.3.1 User Scenario and Fig.3 UI walkthrough, 'Traceability via test suites' and 'Implementation and validation' subsections (p.4).
verbatim_notes: p.2: 'DG3 Decisions are traceable to code. Each decision is formally connected to the implementation, giving programmers a concrete way to validate that the code reflects their intent.' p.3: 'Aporia elicits decisions with questions as an application of QOC.' p.4: 'Every time Nikos commits a decision to the Bank, Aporia generates a test suite to validate the (future) implementation against that decision.' p.2: 'participants... exhibited... 79% lower likelihood of mismatches between their mental model and the actual implementation compared to the baseline coding agent.'

citation: Dhar, R., Vaidhyanathan, K., Varma, V.: AgenticAKM: Enroute to Agentic Architecture Knowledge Management, arXiv preprint (also AGENT'26 workshop @ ICSE 2026, Rio de Janeiro, ACM DOI 10.1145/3786167.3788416), IIIT Hyderabad, submitted 4 Feb 2026.
problem_addressed: Architecture Knowledge Management (AKM) is laborious and often skipped, causing architectural knowledge vaporization; naive single-prompt LLM approaches are ineffective because AK is distributed across code, commits, issue trackers and documentation beyond one prompt's context window. AgenticAKM decomposes AKM into specialized agent roles to automate ADR generation from a code repository.
state_model: No formal ontological/epistemic/lifecycle state triple. The working object is the Architecture Decision Record (ADR), a structured document with standard sections (Title, Context, Decision, Consequences); intermediate state is held in per-agent-group artifacts (repo summaries, issue summaries, document summaries, retrieved specs/diagrams) rather than a unified typed state model.
transition_model: An iterative validation-refinement loop exists (Summary Validator or ADR Validator rejects -> sent back to the Summarizer/Generator for refinement, up to 3 iterations) but this regenerates the artifact rather than appending a typed transition preserving the prior draft; no evidence of retained history of earlier draft versions once a later one is approved.
provenance_model: Weak/implicit: each agent's output is attributable to its role (Repo Summarizer, ADR Generator, etc.), and the ADR Validator can flag 'redundancy or contradiction' against existing ADRs via vector retrieval, but there is no actor/authority/evidence/method/lineage/delegation schema comparable to D-System's H3 -- provenance is pipeline-stage attribution, not a queryable multi-actor graph.
actor_model: A human 'Architect' configures, monitors and can intervene in the workflow via an Orchestrator (Router, Monitor, Interaction Manager, Guardrails, External API Manager); below that, four specialized agent groups (Extractor, Retriever, Generator, Validator) with further sub-agents (e.g. Repo Summarizer, ADR Generator, Org Policy Validator) execute the pipeline. This is a real multi-agent actor topology but hierarchical/orchestrated, not an authority-weighted, independence-aware collective.
temporal_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- no bitemporal or explicit versioning model was described in the sections read (pp.1-4); the paper notes future work would extend to 'longitudinal industrial studies,' implying no such temporal model exists yet.
conflict_trust_mechanism: Narrow: the ADR Validator agent 'may use Vector Retrieval to compare the new ADR against existing ones to check for redundancy or contradiction' -- a real but single-hop, LLM-judged consistency check against a fixed knowledge base, not a general conflict-resolution/trust-weighting mechanism over independently-sourced, possibly-disagreeing evidence (H3/H4).
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no independence-aware corroboration of multiple sources; the pipeline is a single linear (with local retry loops) generation process per repository, evaluated with two different underlying LLMs (Gemini-2.5-pro, GPT-5) as an ablation, not as independent evidence to be reconciled.
memory_model: A project-scoped knowledge base is queried by Retriever agents (ADR Retriever, Architecture Diagram Retriever, Requirement Docs Retriever) via vector retrieval, file-system search and web search; positioned as a retrieval substrate for the pipeline rather than a first-class, versioned memory architecture in its own right.
retrieval_context_model: Tool-mediated retrieval across multiple sources (vector DB of past ADRs/decisions, file system, web search, knowledge base) selected per agent role; context is assembled by role-specific tool calls, not by a topology-aware selection over lineage, dissent, authority or convergence (H5).
decision_representation: Central and closely matching: ADRs are generated with the standard Title/Context/Decision/Consequences structure (the field's canonical decision-plus-rationale template, downstream of the Kruchten/Jansen & Bosch/Farenhorst-de Boer lineage also in this batch, though this paper does not cite that lineage by name) -- directly on D-System's decision-node concept, now agent-authored rather than human-authored.
requirement_derivation: Present but shallow: a 'Requirement Docs Retriever' agent locates and pulls information from requirements documents to ensure generated ADRs 'align with specified project goals,' but requirements are treated as an input constraint to retrieve, not as an object formally derived from a decision (D-System's H7 direction is reversed here: requirements inform decisions, rather than decisions deriving requirements).
specification_representation: A 'Specification Docs Generator' agent (within the Generator group) drafts technical specification documents for new components/services using an LLM, 'ensuring the documentation is detailed, clear, and consistent with the established architecture' -- a real specification-generation mechanism, evaluated less thoroughly than ADR generation in the reported experiment (the paper's Sec.4 experiment instantiates ADR generation specifically, not the full agent roster).
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no phase/plan artifact; the Orchestrator's workflow is a fixed four-stage pipeline with local retry loops, not a multi-step plan object.
execution_unit_session_model: The per-repository ADR-generation run (Extract -> Retrieve -> Generate -> Validate, with up to 3 refinement iterations per validated stage) is the closest analog to an execution unit; it runs end-to-end without human intervention in the reported user study ('the workflow ran without human intervention').
artifact_code_linkage: Direct: the Repo Summarizer agent analyzes the actual codebase (parsed via a Parser/Cloner tool) to ground the summary and, downstream, the generated ADRs and specs in the real repository content -- a working code-to-knowledge linkage, though evaluated only for extraction-into-documentation, not documentation-driving-code-change.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE in the mechanism read -- validation here means LLM-based quality/consistency checking of generated documents (Summary Validator, ADR Validator, Org Policy Validator) against source code and existing documents, not execution of automated tests as in this batch's Aporia source.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no production telemetry loop.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: The Validator agents' reject/refine loop feeds back into the Summarizer/Generator agents within a single run (up to 3 iterations), and approved ADRs are 'saved,' becoming part of the knowledge base future Retriever agents will query -- a real, if narrow and single-session, feedback-into-knowledge mechanism.
forward_traceability: Code repository -> repo/issue/document summaries -> retrieved context -> generated ADR/spec is explicit and automated, covering Artifact -> Decision/Specification in D-System's proposed lifecycle.
backward_traceability: The ADR Validator 'cross-references the summary created by the Extractor against the actual source code to ensure its accuracy and completeness,' giving a working backward check from generated decision documentation to its originating code -- matching D-System's H9 backward direction at the Artifact/Decision boundary.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE beyond the single-hop redundancy/contradiction check in the ADR Validator; no propagation of a changed assumption or evidence source across dependent decisions, requirements or artifacts (H10) was described.
human_agent_scope: Explicitly human-agent collaborative with an 'architect in the loop' as current supervisor and named future-work direction to 'enhance human-agent collaboration... through an architect in the loop model' -- squarely in D-System's agentic framing, published 2026.
implementation_availability: Working research prototype with public source: 'The source code for all the experiments alongside the data used is available on GitHub' at github.com/sa4s-serc/AgenticAKM (read directly from the paper's own footnote); not established in the sections read whether the repository is actively maintained beyond the paper's experiments.
evaluation_method: Within-subjects-style comparative user study across 29 developer-selected repositories (13 participants, 0-6 years experience), 4 configurations (Baseline/Agentic x Gemini-2.5-pro/GPT-5), rated by participants on Relevance, Coherence, Completeness, Conciseness and Overall Quality (1-5 scale); Agentic-GPT-5 and Agentic-Gemini scored highest overall (3.8-3.9) vs. LLM-only baselines (3.3).
strongest_dsystem_overlap: A multi-agent pipeline (Extraction/Retrieval/Generation/Validation) that reads a code repository, retrieves existing architectural knowledge, generates decision records in the field's standard rationale-bearing template, and validates them against source code and prior ADRs with an iterative refinement loop -- a direct 2026 agentic collision with D-System's H6 (integrated human-agent knowledge evolution), H9 (bidirectional decision<->code traceability) and, narrowly, H3/H10 (single-hop contradiction checking and validator-driven refinement).
strongest_difference: No append-only transition history (refinement overwrites drafts rather than preserving prior versions, so H2 is not met), no independence-aware convergence weighting across sources (H4 untouched), no requirement-derived-from-decision direction (H7's core claim runs the opposite way here: requirements are retrieved to constrain decisions, not derived from them), and no deployment/runtime/knowledge-update closure (H11 untouched) -- the system recovers and documents existing architecture from a repository snapshot; it does not model or automate the upstream idea/evidence/reasoning construction that produced that architecture, nor a persistent cross-session knowledge-construction system.
derivative_ancestor: dhar-et-al-draft-architectural-design-decisions-llms-2025 (Dhar, Kakran, Karan, Vaidhyanathan, Varma: DRAFT-ing Architectural Design Decisions using LLMs, arXiv:2504.08207, 11 Apr 2025) -- cited directly by AgenticAKM (Sec.5, 'Dhar et al. [9] explored LLMs' ability to generate architectural decisions from context') as its own authors' prior single-LLM-prompt result, which AgenticAKM extends into a multi-agent pipeline. Not the classical AKM decision-view lineage (jansen-bosch-architecture-as-decisions-wicsa-2005, de-boer-architectural-knowledge-management-dissertation-2009, both elsewhere in this batch): the paper's own Related Works does not cite that lineage by name, despite the ADR template it automates being a direct technical descendant of it.
evidence_locator: Title/authors/venue and Abstract (p.1); Sec.1 Introduction, motivation and four-agent decomposition (p.1); Fig.1 'Agentic AKM' architecture diagram and Sec.3 AKM Agents, subsections 3.1-3.4 describing Extractor/Retriever/Generator/Validator sub-agents (p.2-3); Sec.4.1 'Agentic ADR generation from repository' describing the validation-refinement loop and GitHub footnote (p.3); Sec.4.2-4.3 Evaluation Setup and Results, Table 1 (p.3-4); Sec.5 Related Works (p.4); Sec.6 Conclusion and Future Works (p.4).
verbatim_notes: p.3: 'This summary is then validated by a Summary Validator Agent. If the summary is rejected, it is sent back to the Summarizer for refinement in a loop that runs up to three times.' p.3: 'ADR Validator: This agent scrutinizes generated ADRs for logical consistency, format correctness, and overall quality. It may use Vector Retrieval to compare the new ADR against existing ones to check for redundancy or contradiction.' p.1: 'The source code for all the experiments alongside the data used is available on GitHub.' p.4: 'Future work will... enhance human-agent collaboration through an architect in the loop model.'

citation: Fountas, Z., Benfeghoul, M.A., Oomerjee, A., Christopoulou, F., Lampouras, G., Bou-Ammar, H., Wang, J.: Human-inspired Episodic Memory for Infinite Context LLMs (EM-LLM). Huawei Noah's Ark Lab, London + UCL AI Centre. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025; originally posted as an arXiv preprint 12 Jul 2024, revised through v3 (10 Oct 2025).
problem_addressed: Transformer LLMs struggle to maintain coherence and accuracy over very long contexts, and existing long-context/retrieval methods (RAG, fixed-size token-block retrieval like InfLLM) do not adapt segmentation to content; EM-LLM asks whether organizing an LLM's context the way the human brain organizes continuous experience into episodic events can close this gap with no fine-tuning.
state_model: An 'episodic event' is the state unit: a variable-length, contiguous group of past tokens (KV-cache segment) bounded by detected event boundaries; no ontological/epistemic/lifecycle classification is attached to an event -- it is a similarity/attention-defined token cluster, not a typed knowledge state.
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- events are formed online as new tokens are processed (surprise-based boundary detection, refined by a graph-theoretic cohesion/separation objective) and then persist as fixed evicted-memory units; there is no typed transition between named states, no provenance-carrying edge, and no revision of a formed event after refinement.
provenance_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no actor/authority/evidence/method/lineage/delegation is attached to an event; an event's only 'provenance' is its position in the original token sequence and its attention-key similarity to other tokens.
actor_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- single LLM, single context stream; no multi-actor, multi-agent or stakeholder model.
temporal_model: Implicit only: events retain their original sequential order and are retrieved partly via temporal contiguity/asymmetry effects (favoring items encoded close together in time and in forward succession, per Howard & Kahana 2002's Temporal Context Model) -- a real temporal-recency/contiguity mechanism, but not a bitemporal or explicit versioning model.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no conflicting-claim arbitration; all retained token content is treated as equally valid past context.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no independence-aware corroboration across multiple sources; retrieval strengthens access to similar/temporally-proximate events, not agreement-weighted evidence.
memory_model: The paper's central contribution: context is split into three groups -- attention-sink initial tokens, an evicted-memory pool organized into episodic events via online Bayesian-surprise segmentation refined by graph-theoretic boundary optimization (treating attention-key similarity as a weighted adjacency matrix to maximize within-event cohesion and cross-event separation, O(nm) complexity), and a local-context working-memory window. This is a concrete, evaluated, human-inspired episodic memory architecture for LLM context management.
retrieval_context_model: Two-stage retrieval: (1) similarity-based k-NN retrieval of relevant events/token-groups, combined with (2) temporally-contiguous and temporally-asymmetric retrieval favoring events near the current position and forward-succession order, mirroring human free-recall dynamics -- a genuine, cognitive-science-grounded retrieval mechanism, but keyed on token/attention similarity and recency rather than reasoning lineage, supporting evidence, dissent, authority or convergence as D-System's H5 proposes.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no decision object exists in this architecture.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- operates within a single continuous LLM context/session; no phase or session boundary object beyond the token stream itself.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not a software-artifact system; 'events' are token-sequence segments, not code or build artifacts. (A separate implementation repository exists at github.com/em-llm/EM-LLM-model, but that is the paper's own code, not a code-linkage mechanism within the method.)
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- events, once formed and refined, are not updated by later evidence; there is no knowledge-revision loop, only continued accumulation and retrieval of past token groups.
forward_traceability: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no forward-derivation chain (idea -> decision -> requirement -> ... ) exists in this architecture.
backward_traceability: NOT_APPLICABLE in D-System's sense -- a retrieved event can be traced back to its original token positions and surprise/boundary-refinement scores, but this is positional/statistical traceability within one token stream, not reasoning-to-evidence traceability.
human_agent_scope: NOT_APPLICABLE / out of scope -- purely a model-internal context-management mechanism; no human or agent actor is modeled by the method itself (a human is only the end user of the LLM being augmented).
implementation_availability: Publicly available: official code at github.com/em-llm/EM-LLM-model (read directly from the paper's own footnote, 'Code available at: https://github.com/em-llm/EM-LLM-model'), applied to pretrained LLMs (e.g. LLaMA-3.1-8B) with no fine-tuning required.
evaluation_method: Benchmarked on LongBench and an extended INFINITY-Bench (up to 10M tokens, passkey retrieval), compared against InfLLM (prior SOTA retrieval baseline), RAG (NV-Embed-v2 retriever) and full-context models across multiple LLMs; also validated event-segmentation quality against human-annotated podcast transcripts and the PG-19 long-book corpus, finding correlation between EM-LLM event boundaries and human-perceived event boundaries.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: A rigorously evaluated, cognitive-science-grounded mechanism for segmenting continuous experience into bounded episodic units and retrieving them via a combined similarity-plus-temporal-contiguity process -- directly relevant precedent for any 'episodic memory for agents' or 'topology-aware context transfer' claim (H5), now a peer-reviewed ICLR 2025 result with 10M-token demonstrated scale and a public implementation.
strongest_difference: No knowledge-state ontology, no provenance, no actor/authority model, no decision/requirement/artifact/verification linkage, and no reasoning-lineage-, evidence-, dissent-, authority- or convergence-aware retrieval -- EM-LLM organizes and retrieves raw token history for one LLM's own context window; it is a memory-retrieval subsystem for context management, not a knowledge-construction or software-development architecture, and H5's epistemic dimensions (dissent, authority, convergence, unresolved uncertainty) are entirely outside its scope.
derivative_ancestor: kurby-zacks-segmentation-perception-memory-events-2008 (already inventoried, D23) -- EM-LLM's own Sec.1 and Sec.2.2 name Zacks & Swallow's Event Segmentation Theory (2007), Baldassano et al.'s event-structure-discovery work (Neuron, 2017) and Howard & Kahana's Temporal Context Model (2002) as the direct cognitive-science ancestors of its surprise-based segmentation and temporal-contiguity retrieval mechanisms -- a 2024/2025 computational instantiation of a 2002-2017 memory-science lineage, not an independent invention.
evidence_locator: Title/authors/affiliations and 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' header (p.1); Abstract (p.1); Sec.1 Introduction, Contributions paragraph describing (a) surprise-based boundary detection, (b) graph-theoretic refinement O(nm), (c) two-stage similarity+temporal-contiguity retrieval (pp.2-3); Sec.2.1 comparison to InfLLM/RAG/k-NN retrieval methods (p.3); Sec.2.2 'Neural models of Episodic Memory and Event Cognition' citing Zacks/Baldassano/Howard & Kahana (p.4); Sec.3.1 Architecture, three-group context structure (initial/evicted/local tokens) (p.4); Fig.1 benchmark results (LongBench, extended Retrieve.PassKey to 10M tokens) (p.2).

citation: Al Manir, S., Niestroy, J., Levinson, M.A., Clark, T.: Evidence Graphs: Supporting Transparent and FAIR Computation, with Defeasible Reasoning on Data, Methods, and Results. bioRxiv preprint, posted 2021; also published as a peer-reviewed chapter in Provenance and Annotation of Data and Processes: 8th/9th International Provenance and Annotation Workshop (IPAW 2020+2021), Springer LNCS vol.12839, 2021.
problem_addressed: Computational results in science are often accepted at face value even though the underlying data, methods and software are rarely re-examined; FAIR principles improve findability/accessibility/interoperability/reusability of data and software but do not, by themselves, represent whether a result's supporting evidence has since been challenged or undermined. Evidence Graphs (EVI) extend provenance with defeasible-argumentation relations so that support and challenge among computational results, data and methods are first-class, machine-reasoned facts.
state_model: Entities are typed as PROV-O subclasses: Representation (subclass of prov:Entity), Material, Method, Dataset, Software, Instrument, Image, Article, Claim, plus EvidenceGraph itself as a first-class computational object; no separate ontological/epistemic/lifecycle triple beyond PROV-O's own Entity/Activity/Agent typing, extended with these domain classes.
transition_model: Not a state-transition log in D-System's S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 sense; instead, a static/growing graph of typed argumentation edges (supports, directlySupports, challenges, directlyChallenges) with two inference rules: support propagates transitively, and 'if C challenges A and A supports B, then C challenges B' -- propagation is logical/deductive over the graph via an OWL 2 reasoner, not a temporal sequence of typed state transitions.
provenance_model: Very close conceptually: EVI is explicitly 'an extension of W3C PROV, based on argumentation theory,' where all supports/challenges relations are declared subproperties of PROV relations (e.g. directlySupports generalizes usedBy and generates); every node carries a persistent ARK identifier resolving to the cited object. This is a real, OWL-formalized, production-deployed provenance model directly on D-System's H3 territory -- evidence and lineage are explicit -- but it omits H3's authority/delegation dimensions and, critically, its conflict-resolution step.
actor_model: PROV-O's Agent taxonomy (Person, Organization, SoftwareAgent), with a 'Service usedBy a Computation' modeled as a kind of SoftwareAgent; attribution is treated as a statement's 'simplest supporting evidence' (an explicit ethos/character-of-speaker argument), but there is no authority-weighting or domain-expertise scoring across actors.
temporal_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- no bitemporal or explicit versioning model was found in the sections read; evidence graphs accumulate nodes as new computations/challenges are recorded (17,996 nodes in the reported NICU deployment) but no valid-time/transaction-time distinction was described.
conflict_trust_mechanism: The single most important finding for D-System's H3: EVI explicitly declines to auto-resolve conflicts. 'Challenges do not invalidate, they present an opposing view. They ultimately require human judgment as to their validity and strength.' The mechanism surfaces and propagates conflict (a challenge to A undercuts anything A supports) but stops short of computing a trust/authority-weighted resolution -- this is a deliberate design choice the paper defends, not an oversight, and directly bounds how far this source can be read as falsifying H3.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE in the sections read -- no independence-aware corroboration weighting (e.g. discounting derivative agreement) was described; multiple supports simply accumulate as transitive support edges.
memory_model: The EvidenceGraph is itself a persistent, queryable, first-class computational object, stored and reasoned over in a Stardog RDF quad store (which performs the OWL inferencing), with results archived to institutional Dataverse repositories -- a genuine persistent memory architecture for evidence, at production scale.
retrieval_context_model: A custom 'PATH query,' extending SPARQL, generates an EvidenceGraph DAG rooted at a given object, letting a user retrieve the full chain of supporting/challenging evidence for a result -- lineage-aware retrieval, though not weighted by dissent, authority or convergence beyond the raw graph structure.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no decision object; the domain is scientific/computational claims and their supporting evidence, not software-development or organizational decisions.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; out of the paper's scope.
execution_unit_session_model: A Computation (a PROV Activity) using specific Datasets/Software/Instruments and producing a Claim/Image/Article is the closest analog to an execution unit, but it is a completed scientific computation, not a session or development phase.
artifact_code_linkage: Direct: Software and Method are first-class EVI classes linked into the evidence graph alongside the Data they operated on and the Results/Claims they produced, all resolvable via persistent ARK identifiers -- a real, working artifact/data/method linkage, though for computational science reproducibility rather than application source code.
test_verification_linkage: Indirect: a 'challenge' to a Claim functions as a verification-relevant signal (an opposing view on the result's validity) propagated through the graph, but this is human-authored argumentative challenge, not automated test execution.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no software deployment concept.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE in the software-runtime sense, though the entire ontology is arguably about runtime (computational-execution) evidence for scientific results specifically -- Results/Claims generated by a Computation are exactly this kind of 'runtime evidence' for the claims it supports.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: Yes, directly: challenges recorded against a Claim propagate (via the challenge-propagation inference rule) to everything that Claim supports, so new evidence updates the graph's derivable state for all dependent claims -- a real, if manually-authored-challenge-triggered, feedback-to-knowledge mechanism.
forward_traceability: Data/Method/Software -> Computation -> Claim/Result is explicit and machine-traversable via the EvidenceGraph and PATH query.
backward_traceability: A Claim/Result can be traced back through directlySupports/supports edges to its originating data, methods and software, and further back to any challenges bearing on those -- a strong, working, graph-native backward trace closely matching D-System's H9 backward direction, within the scientific-evidence domain rather than the software-development domain.
change_impact_mechanism: Partial and directly relevant to H10: the challenge-propagation inference rule ('if C challenges A and A supports B, then C challenges B') is exactly a narrow-scope epistemic blast-radius computation -- a new challenge to one piece of evidence automatically flags every claim transitively supported by it as now-contested, though it stops at flagging, not at re-deriving or reassessing those downstream claims.
human_agent_scope: Human/organizational/software-agent scope (Person, Organization, SoftwareAgent per PROV-O), in a computational-science reproducibility setting; not an AI-agentic system, and the paper is explicit that resolving a flagged conflict is left to human judgment.
implementation_availability: Production-grade and publicly available: the EVI ontology (OWL 2) is published at https://w3id.org/EVI# under MIT license with a GitHub-archived OWL file and Zenodo archival; deployed via the FAIRSCAPE microservices framework, backed by a Stardog RDF quad store performing the OWL inferencing, and evaluated on a real NICU physiological time-series study spanning 5,957 infants, producing a 17,996-node evidence graph.
evaluation_method: Real-world deployment case study (NICU time-series data across 5,957 infants, FAIRSCAPE-generated evidence graph of 17,996 nodes) rather than a controlled comparative experiment; evaluated on scale/tractability of the ontology and inference rules in production, not on a held-out benchmark.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: An OWL-formalized, PROV-O-extended ontology (EVI) making support and challenge relations among computational results, data, methods and software first-class, transitively-propagating, machine-reasoned graph edges, deployed at real scale with persistent identifiers and SPARQL-based lineage queries -- structurally the closest single match in this batch to D-System's H2 (typed transitions preserving reasoning/evidence relationships) and H3 (provenance as conflict-relevant input), and a working precedent for H9's backward-traceability and H10's narrow blast-radius propagation.
strongest_difference: Deliberately and explicitly does not perform authority-weighted arbitration or trust-scored conflict resolution -- 'they ultimately require human judgment' -- so it does not falsify H3's automated-arbitration claim even though it strongly precedes H3's provenance-representation claim; no independence-aware convergence weighting (H4), no decision/requirement/specification/plan software-development lifecycle at all (confined to the scientific-evidence/Knowledge Construction side of D-System's proposed two-system split), and no AI-agentic actors.
derivative_ancestor: aba-argumentation-theoretic-default-reasoning-1997 and pollock-defeasible-reasoning-oscar-2000 (both already inventoried in D11, adjacent but not identical) -- the paper's own Methods section cites its direct argumentation-theory ancestors by name: Dung, P.M., On the Acceptability of Arguments..., Artificial Intelligence 77, 1995 (the foundational abstract-argumentation-framework paper cited by both already-inventoried D11 rows); Cayrol, C. & Lagasquie-Schiex, M.C., On the Acceptability of Arguments in Bipolar Argumentation Frameworks, 2005 (origin of a formal 'support' relation alongside Dung's 'attack'); and Toulmin, S.E., The Uses of Argument, 1958 (claim/data/warrant/backing/qualifier/rebuttal argument structure). EVI is a 2021 PROV-O-grounded, OWL-formalized instantiation of this 1958-2005 lineage, not an independent invention of evidence-as-argument.
evidence_locator: bioRxiv v3 full-text HTML: Introduction ('Results, methods, reasoning, computations, and interpretations may be challenged by others in the community'); Methods section defining EVI classes/relations and stating 'EVI is an extension of W3C PROV, based on argumentation theory, which enables defeasible reasoning about computations, their results, data, and software,' and the two property-chain inference rules; Discussion section on FAIR/reproducibility motivation and the human-judgment limitation on challenges; Implementation section describing the w3id.org/EVI# ontology, FAIRSCAPE deployment, Stardog quad store, PATH query, and the 17,996-node/5,957-infant NICU case study. Venue/peer-review status confirmed via link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-80960-7 (IPAW 2020+2021 proceedings, LNCS 12839) -- the Springer chapter itself is paywalled (303 redirect to institutional login on direct fetch), so venue/DOI confirmation is via the book's public landing page and search-engine-indexed metadata, not a full read of the Springer version of record.
verbatim_notes: 'EVI is an extension of W3C PROV, based on argumentation theory, which enables defeasible reasoning about computations, their results, data, and software.' 'if C challenges A and A supports B, then C challenges B.' 'A challenge to A's supporting evidence undercuts A -- it reduces the warrant for belief in A.' 'Challenges do not invalidate, they present an opposing view. They ultimately require human judgment as to their validity and strength.' 'every node in the graph has a persistent identifier, based on the ARK system.'

citation: Park, Y.B.: Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents: Formal Belief Revision Semantics for Versioned Memory Architectures (Kumiho). Kumiho Inc. arXiv preprint, 18 Mar 2026 (in-body date 17 Mar 2026), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
problem_addressed: AI agents increasingly produce substantial outputs (code, designs, documents, intermediate results) across multi-agent workflows, but existing agent-memory systems handle versioning, retrieval and consolidation as separate, under-formalized components; the paper argues cognitive memory (remembering, tracking belief evolution, recalling why decisions were made) and work-product management (versioning, locating, linking agent outputs) share identical structural primitives and can be unified in one graph-native architecture formally grounded in belief revision theory.
state_model: A belief/memory item is an immutable versioned graph snapshot (a revision) addressed by a dereferenceable URI, with a mutable tag pointer indicating which revision is 'current' -- structurally close to D-System's state abstraction, though framed as belief-base contents (Hansson 1999) over ground triples rather than an explicit ontological/epistemic/lifecycle (O,E,L) triple.
transition_model: Directly on-target: immutable revisions plus typed dependency edges plus mutable tag pointers instantiate a formally-grounded transition model. The paper proves the graph operations satisfy AGM postulates K*2-K*6 and Hansson's Relevance/Core-Retainment belief-base postulates, explicitly rejects the AGM Recovery postulate ('a principled rejection... grounded in immutable versioning'), and leaves supplementary postulates K*7/K*8 open -- this is the closest match in this batch to D-System's S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 typed, provenance-carrying, append-only transition claim (H2), scoped to a simple propositional logic over ground triples rather than D-System's full generality.
provenance_model: Strong: 'every agent belief has a URI, a revision history, provenance edges to source evidence, and an immutable audit trail.' Provenance edges link beliefs/work-products to the reasoning or evidence that produced them, and revisions are citable and traceable end-to-end -- close to D-System's H3 in structure (lineage, evidence, immutability) though the paper does not describe an explicit actor-authority/delegation weighting scheme beyond the provenance-edge and audit-trail mechanism.
actor_model: Human operators and AI agents share the same graph, SDK and inspection tools ('agents use the same graph to remember, to find each other's outputs, and to build upon them... human operators audit the entire chain with the same SDK and inspection tools'); the paper explicitly cites governance/accountability motivations (ISACA's 2025 agentic-AI audit analysis on identity management, decision traceability and accountability gaps; IBM's 'Agent Decision Records' -- a directly parallel, independently-coined agent-decision-record concept worth noting alongside this batch's Aporia and AgenticAKM decision-record mechanisms) but does not describe authority-weighted arbitration among multiple actors.
temporal_model: Versioned/immutable-revision temporality (each revision is a permanent, addressable snapshot; a mutable tag pointer tracks 'current') is explicit, but the paper does not describe a bitemporal (valid-time vs. transaction-time) model distinctly from this revision-history mechanism.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS in the sections read (pp.1-3) -- belief revision (AGM K*2-K*6) inherently concerns incorporating new, possibly-conflicting information, but the specific mechanism for detecting and adjudicating conflicting beliefs was not reached in this pass; Sections 7 and 9 (belief-revision correspondence, safety-hardened consolidation) were not read in full.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS in the sections read -- not described in the Abstract/Introduction; would require reading Section 7 (formal belief-base correspondence) in full.
memory_model: The paper's central contribution: a dual-store architecture (Redis working memory + Neo4j long-term property graph) with hybrid full-text/vector retrieval, an asynchronous consolidation pipeline (with published-item protection, circuit breakers, dry-run validation, auditable cursor-based resumption), formally grounded in AGM/Hansson belief revision -- a concrete, benchmarked, production-oriented cognitive memory architecture.
retrieval_context_model: Three named innovations: (1) prospective indexing -- LLM-generated hypothetical future query scenarios indexed alongside each memory summary at write time, to bridge a cue-trigger semantic gap at recall time; (2) event extraction -- structured events with consequences appended to summaries to preserve causal detail narrative compression would drop; (3) client-side LLM reranking -- the consuming agent's own LLM selects the most relevant sibling revision from structured metadata at zero extra inference cost. This is a real, non-trivial retrieval architecture, though keyed on semantic/temporal cues and revision metadata rather than D-System's proposed lineage/dissent/authority/convergence weighting (H5).
decision_representation: Present conceptually ('recall why decisions were made' is named as a core cognitive-memory requirement, and IBM's 'Agent Decision Records' are cited as an industry parallel) but no explicit decision-object schema was read in the sections covered (pp.1-3); Sections 4-6 (architecture, asset management extensions) were not read in full.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE in the sections read -- not addressed as a distinct concept from work-product versioning.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE in the sections read -- not addressed.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE in the sections read -- not addressed; the architecture is memory/versioning infrastructure, not a planning system.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- multi-agent pipelines are described at a high level ('a coding agent writes and commits code... a research agent gathers, synthesizes, and reports findings') but no explicit session/phase-boundary object was read in the sections covered.
artifact_code_linkage: Direct and a named architectural goal: the same graph that stores agent memories also manages agent 'work products' (code, designs, documents, intermediate results), each versioned, URI-addressable and linked via typed edges back to the reasoning/inputs that produced it -- closely matching D-System's H7/H9 claims about linking implementation outputs to the reasoning that generated them, evaluated empirically for the memory side (Section 15) but noted as 'planned as future work' for the multi-agent asset-management validation specifically.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE in the sections read -- not addressed as a test/verification concept; 'automated AGM compliance testing (49 scenarios, 7 postulates)' validates the formal belief-revision claims themselves, not software test/verification linkage.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed in the sections read.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: The asynchronous consolidation pipeline (extending 'prior sleep-time compute approaches') consolidates accumulating memory into the graph with safety guards, functioning as a feedback-into-knowledge mechanism, though the mechanism's detail (Section 9) was not read in full in this pass.
forward_traceability: Explicit: 'downstream agents locate inputs via URI resolution, track which revision is current via tag pointers, and link their own outputs back via typed edges' -- a real, working forward-traceability mechanism across a multi-agent pipeline.
backward_traceability: Explicit: provenance edges trace a belief/work-product back to source evidence, and 'every provenance chain is traceable' via the URI addressing scheme -- directly matching D-System's H9 backward direction.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS in the sections read -- belief revision inherently implies downstream consequences of a changed belief, but the specific propagation/impact mechanism (if any) was not reached in this pass.
human_agent_scope: Explicitly human-agent collaborative, framed around multi-agent pipelines (coding, design, research, production-coordination agents) with human operators auditing via the same SDK -- squarely 2026 agentic scope, directly citing enterprise agent-governance concerns (ISACA, IBM Agent Decision Records).
implementation_availability: Partially open, partially commercial: the core graph server is a paid cloud service (kumiho.io); the Python SDK, MCP memory plugin, and benchmark suite are open-source at github.com/KumihoIO. A working, benchmarked, production-marketed system, not merely a research prototype.
evaluation_method: LoCoMo benchmark (token-level F1 with Porter stemming): 0.447 four-category F1 (n=1,540, 'highest reported score across the retrieval categories'), 97.5% adversarial refusal accuracy (n=446), overall F1 0.565 including adversarial (n=1,986); LoCoMo-Plus (a Level-2 cognitive-memory benchmark for implicit constraint recall under cue-trigger semantic disconnect): 93.3% judge accuracy (n=401) as author-reported, though the paper itself discloses that 'independent reproduction by the benchmark authors yielded results in the mid-80% range' -- still outperforming the best published baseline (Gemini 2.5 Pro, 45.7%) but a material self-disclosed reproducibility gap on the paper's own strongest claimed number. Automated AGM compliance testing: 49 scenarios, 7 postulates, 100% operational adherence claimed.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: A graph-native memory architecture combining immutable versioned revisions, typed dependency/provenance edges, mutable tag pointers and URI-based addressing, formally proven to satisfy several AGM/Hansson belief-revision postulates, explicitly unifying cognitive memory with work-product/artifact versioning so that agent outputs are 'automatically versioned, addressable, and linked to the reasoning that produced them' -- the closest single match in this batch to D-System's H2 (typed transition semantics preserving reasoning memory) and a strong precedent for H7/H9 (development-provenance linkage and bidirectional traceability), at production/commercial maturity with published (if partially unreproduced) benchmark results.
strongest_difference: Formal correspondence is explicitly partial and scoped -- proven only for a 'deliberately simple propositional logic over ground triples,' with the Recovery postulate rejected by design and K*7/K*8 left open -- so it does not claim the full generality of D-System's proposed state/transition model; no described conflict-arbitration, independence-aware convergence, or epistemic-blast-radius mechanism was read in the sections covered; the paper is explicit that it synthesizes rather than invents ('we contribute not novel individual components... but a novel architectural synthesis'), and the strongest reported benchmark result (LoCoMo-Plus 93.3%) carries a self-disclosed independent-reproduction gap (mid-80% range) that bounds how strongly its empirical claims should be weighted.
derivative_ancestor: Alchourron, C.E., Gardenfors, P., Makinson, D.: On the Logic of Theory Change: Partial Meet Contraction and Revision Functions, Journal of Symbolic Logic 50(2), 1985 (the AGM postulates, the paper's own named 'central formal contribution' ancestor); also Hansson, S.O., belief base theory (1999) and Flouris, G. et al., description-logic AGM impossibility results (2005), both cited directly by the paper as the scoping constraints its correspondence proof works within. The paper additionally self-identifies as a synthesis of concurrent 2025 systems (Graphiti, Mem0, A-MEM) rather than a component-level invention.
evidence_locator: Title/author/affiliation and license (p.1); Abstract (p.1-2), including AGM correspondence claim, LoCoMo/LoCoMo-Plus results and the independent-reproduction disclosure; Sec.1 Introduction, 'cognitive memory' vs. 'work product management' framing and the five numbered contributions (pp.2-3), including item 2 'Formal belief base revision correspondence' pointing to Section 7, and item 1 quoting the Graphiti/Mem0/A-MEM concurrent-systems disclaimer. Sections 4-9 and 15 (architecture detail, formal proofs, safety-hardened consolidation, full benchmark methodology) were not read in this pass and are recorded as NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS above where relevant.
verbatim_notes: 'The central formal contribution is a correspondence between the AGM belief revision framework [Alchourron et al. 1985] and the operational semantics of a property graph memory system... proving satisfaction of the basic AGM postulates (K*2-K*6) and Hansson's belief base postulates (Relevance, Core-Retainment), while providing a principled rejection of the Recovery postulate grounded in immutable versioning.' 'every agent belief has a URI, a revision history, provenance edges to source evidence, and an immutable audit trail.' 'independent reproduction by the benchmark authors yielded results in the mid-80% range.' 'We contribute not novel individual components... but a novel architectural synthesis grounded in formal analysis.'

citation: Jansen, A., Bosch, J.: Software Architecture as a Set of Architectural Design Decisions, Proceedings of the 5th IEEE/IFIP Working Conference on Software Architecture (WICSA 2005), pp.109-119, November 2005. (Read via the open-access republication as Chapter 4 of Jansen's 2008 PhD dissertation, University of Groningen; the WICSA proceedings version itself is paywalled on IEEE Xplore.)
problem_addressed: Software architectures have high costs of change, are complex, and erode during evolution, partly because knowledge about the design decisions an architecture is based on is only implicitly embedded in the architecture and 'vaporizes' rather than being explicitly represented; the paper proposes viewing software architecture itself as a composition of explicit architectural design decisions, not just components and connectors.
state_model: An architectural design decision is formally defined: 'A description of the set of architectural additions, subtractions and modifications to the software architecture, the rationale, and the design rules, design constraints and additional requirements that (partially) realize one or more requirements on a given architecture.' The paper's Archium meta-model further formalizes this as a Problem (with Motivation, Cause) resolved by a chosen Solution (Decision, with a Trade-off), resulting in an Architectural Modification that changes the Context (Requirements + other architectural design decisions) -- a genuine, diagrammed (Fig.4.1) conceptual state model for the decision unit itself, close to D-System's decision-node concept though without an O/E/L classification.
transition_model: Directly relevant: 'software architicture = dd1 + dd2 + ... + ddn' -- architecture is explicitly defined as the literal sum/composition of design decisions accumulated over time, and Archium models new functionality as 'a change of nothing to something,' i.e. designing using change rather than merely tracking it. This is a compositional, additive, near-append-only conception of architecture-as-accumulated-decisions -- the closest match in this batch to D-System's H2 framing among the non-formal (i.e. non-AGM-proven) sources, though it lacks a typed provenance-carrying edge on each addition.
provenance_model: Each decision's Rationale, Design rules and Design constraints are explicit, first-class fields, and design rules/constraints 'have a steering influence on future design decisions' -- a real dependency/influence relationship among decisions -- but no actor/authority/evidence/method/delegation schema was found in the sections read; provenance is the decision's own stated rationale, not a multi-actor attribution graph.
actor_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS in the sections read (Ch.4.1-4.5, pp.79-86) -- the paper is written from the architect's perspective throughout but does not describe a multi-stakeholder or multi-actor model in the sections covered; later sections (4.6 case study, 4.7 related work) were not read in this pass.
temporal_model: NOT_APPLICABLE / not addressed as a bitemporal model -- the additive dd1+dd2+...+ddn framing implies decisions accumulate over the architecture's history, but no explicit valid-time/transaction-time distinction or decision-versioning mechanism was described.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; the paper focuses on representing decisions explicitly, not on arbitrating between conflicting ones (design-rule violation is named as a problem the approach helps detect, not a mechanism for resolving competing decisions).
memory_model: Archium itself -- 'first class architectural design decisions... can be communicated, related and reasoned about' -- functions as the persistent representation/memory of an architecture's decision history, addressing the 'knowledge vaporization' problem directly; no separate retrieval/query mechanism was described in the sections read.
retrieval_context_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS in the sections read -- Section 4.6 (case study with 'various views' for visualizing decisions) was not read in this pass and likely addresses this most directly.
decision_representation: Central and closely matching: decisions are formally modeled as first-class objects with Problem/Motivation/Cause, candidate Solutions with Description/Design rules/Design constraints/Consequences/Pros/Cons, a chosen Decision with its Trade-off, and a resulting Architectural Modification -- one of the most formally elaborated decision models in this batch, directly ancestral to the ADR template used by this batch's dhar-vaidhyanathan-varma-agenticakm-2026-arxiv source (Title/Context/Decision/Consequences).
requirement_derivation: A direct, explicit H7 match: 'A design decision may result in additional requirements to be satisfied by the architecture. These new requirements need to be addressed by additional design decisions' (Sec.4.2, 'Additional requirements') -- decisions deriving new requirements, in the same direction D-System's H7 proposes, stated in 2005.
specification_representation: Design rules and design constraints ('prescriptions for further design decisions... mandatory guidelines' and 'limitations on further design... prohibit certain behaviors') function as a lightweight specification mechanism binding subsequent decisions, though not a distinct specification-document artifact.
