citation: Keim, J., Kaplan, A.: From Scattered to Structured: A Vision for Automating Architectural Knowledge Management. In Proceedings of the International Conference on Software Engineering Companion (ICSE-C '26), Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, Apr 12-18 2026. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 5 pages. Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), Germany.
source_type: conference (accepted ICSE-C '26 Companion short vision/position paper -- carries ACM Reference Format, ISBN 978-1-4503-XXXX-X and a DOI placeholder for the venue; inventory's source_type column lists 'preprint', which this source-page read corrects)
problem_addressed: Architectural knowledge (decisions, rationale, structure) is scattered across heterogeneous artifacts (requirements docs, diagrams, code, docs, and -- in the long-term vision -- meeting/call recordings); as systems evolve these artifacts drift out of sync, causing 'architectural erosion' and expensive comprehension/maintenance cost. The paper proposes (not yet builds) an automated pipeline to extract, link, reconcile and consolidate this knowledge into one structured KB supporting conformance checking, change-impact analysis and NL question-answering.
state_model: No formal ontological/epistemic/lifecycle state triple and none proposed even at vision level. The unit of knowledge is an unspecified 'architectural knowledge' entity extracted per-artifact-type into 'a unified knowledge representation schema' (Sec.3.2) -- schema design is listed as future work, not defined in this paper.
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no typed S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 transition semantics proposed. Sec.4 ('Temporal validity and system evolution') explicitly names the problem D-System's transition model addresses (whether to discard superseded knowledge or keep a temporal, versioned KB) but states only that this 'requires sophisticated mechanisms to track changes over time' -- named as an open challenge, no mechanism designed.
provenance_model: Partial and vision-only: 'Update' and 'Validate' arrows in Fig.1 imply extracted knowledge is attributed to its source artifact and to LLM-assisted extraction, and Sec.3.4 has the monitoring agent flag 'ambiguities or conflicts that require domain expertise' to a human; but no actor/authority/evidence/method/lineage provenance schema is defined, and no data model is given for what a provenance record would contain.
actor_model: Two roles only, both human: 'architects' and 'developers' (Sec.1, Sec.3.4), plus the LLM agent itself as a non-human actor that extracts, monitors, and asks clarifying questions. No multi-agent, multi-stakeholder or authority-weighted model -- single KB, single monitoring agent, human validators undifferentiated by role/authority.
temporal_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS as a designed mechanism -- Sec.4 'Temporal validity and system evolution' is the paper's own explicit statement that it has NOT yet determined whether/how to version the KB over time ('The approach must address whether to discard outdated information... or to maintain a temporal knowledge base with versioning and time-aware query capabilities'); this is scoped as unresolved future work, not a gap in this review's access.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no conflicting-evidence arbitration or trust-weighting mechanism; inconsistencies are between artifacts (doc vs. code), not between competing claims/sources, and resolution is 'semi-automated... involve human architects in critical decisions' (Sec.3.3) with no scoring/arbitration logic specified.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no independence-aware corroboration mechanism; not addressed anywhere in the 7 pages.
memory_model: The structured KB itself is the memory model -- a single consolidated, continuously updated knowledge graph/base (exact structure undefined) fed by continuous artifact monitoring (Sec.3.4); positioned as project/team memory, not agent conversational or episodic memory.
retrieval_context_model: RAG over the KB (Sec.3.5), 'analogous to systems for scientific knowledge retrieval such as HubLink' (Sec.1, citing the same author group's 2025 HubLink paper) -- graph-based retrieval combined with LLM generation for NL QA over architectural knowledge; not topology-aware in D-System's sense (no lineage/dissent/authority/convergence signals mentioned as retrieval inputs), and unevaluated (evaluation is future work, Sec.3.5).
decision_representation: Central to the paper's motivating examples: architectural 'decisions and their justifications' are one of the four named artifact types the pipeline extracts from documentation (Sec.1), and consistency checking explicitly targets 'contradictions in architectural decisions' (Sec.3.3); but decisions are extracted/mined from existing text, not created as first-class structured objects with their own persistent record, alternatives, or status field -- no decision schema is given.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- requirements documents are named only as one of the four heterogeneous input-artifact types to mine architectural knowledge from (Sec.1, Sec.2); the paper does not model requirements as derived from decisions or as an output of any process.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; 'specification' does not appear as a system concept, only architecture documentation generally.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no phase/plan/task artifact; 'Planned Steps' (Sec.3) describes the authors' own research roadmap for building the system, not a planning primitive within the envisioned system itself.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no execution-unit or session concept; the agent 'continuously monitors' (Sec.3.4) rather than operating within bounded phases/sessions.
artifact_code_linkage: Direct and explicit, though only in one direction (docs/diagrams -> knowledge, not knowledge -> generated code): code is one of the four artifact types from which 'structural and behavioral knowledge' is statically extracted (Sec.3.1); the KB does not generate or modify code.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- 'test cases' are named once in passing (Sec.2, as one artifact type that embeds knowledge in the SE literature generally) but are not a designed input/output of this paper's own pipeline; no verification-linkage mechanism proposed.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no deployment concept anywhere in the 7 pages.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; the pipeline monitors static artifacts (docs, code, diagrams, recordings) via 'file system monitoring and version control integration' (Sec.3.4), not running-system telemetry, incidents or production observability.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: Partial: the agent 'updates the knowledge base in real-time' (Sec.1) as new/changed artifacts are detected, and unresolved ambiguities are escalated to humans whose answers presumably update the KB (Sec.3.4) -- but this is artifact-change-driven KB maintenance, not a runtime-evidence-to-knowledge loop; no observed-behavior-contradicts-expectation mechanism (D-System Sec.5 of two_system_architecture.md) is described.
forward_traceability: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS as a designed mechanism -- TLR ('traceability techniques from previous work', Sec.3.2) is stated as the linking method but no forward idea/decision->requirement->...->runtime chain is modeled; the paper's scope stops at architecture-documentation artifacts.
backward_traceability: Yes, as a named target capability: 'architecture conformance checking' (Sec.1, Sec.3.2) requires tracing from architecture/code back to documented decisions and requirements, and the Question Detail View concept from HubLink-style QA (Sec.3.5) lets a user query 'why' knowledge exists -- but no backward-trace data model or worked example is given in this 7-page vision paper.
change_impact_mechanism: Named directly as a target capability -- 'change impact analysis' appears three times (Sec.1, Sec.2.1, Sec.3.2) as one of the KB's supported activities -- but is entirely unspecified: no mechanism, algorithm, or even a sketch of how impact would propagate through the KB is given anywhere in the paper; it is a stated goal, not a mechanism.
human_agent_scope: Human-agent collaborative and explicit: 'architects and developers' as human roles plus one 'intelligent agent' (Sec.1) that extracts knowledge, monitors artifacts, detects inconsistencies, and asks clarifying questions before executing KB-impacting actions, 'ensuring that critical decisions remain under human control' (Sec.1) -- published 2026, squarely contemporary with D-System's agentic framing.
implementation_availability: None -- pure vision/position paper. Every mechanism is stated as future work ('we will develop', 'we plan to develop', 'the expected outcome is'); no prototype, code, or artifact exists as of this publication. Sec.3 is literally titled 'Planned Steps.'
evaluation_method: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no evaluation was conducted; Sec.3 states repeatedly that the authors 'will empirically evaluate each step' as future work, and Sec.3.5 states they 'will evaluate the system's ability to answer common architectural queries' -- both prospective, not reported.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: Independently converges on several of D-System's own claims as *open research goals*, not solved mechanisms: an agent-maintained, continuously-updated knowledge base spanning heterogeneous artifact types (echoing H6's ambition, scoped to architecture-documentation rather than full idea-to-runtime lifecycle); change-impact analysis over that KB as an explicit target capability (H10); bidirectional doc<->code traceability via TLR (H9, partial); and -- most strikingly for thesis discipline -- Sec.4 names D-System's own core unsolved design question near-verbatim ('whether to discard outdated information... or maintain a temporal knowledge base with versioning and time-aware query capabilities') as an acknowledged open challenge, confirming the problem is recognized in contemporary literature even though neither paper has a working answer.
strongest_difference: No formal state/transition/provenance model (none proposed, not merely none read); scope is architecture-documentation artifacts only, not D-System's full idea->decision->requirement->specification->plan->execution->artifact->verification->deployment->runtime->knowledge lifecycle -- requirements, specifications, plans, execution sessions, tests, deployment and runtime telemetry are entirely absent from this paper's scope; no working system, code, or evaluation exists to compare against; single-KB single-agent architecture with no multi-actor authority/conflict/convergence model.
derivative_ancestor: Keim, Corallo, Fuchss, Koziolek: Detecting Inconsistencies in Software Architecture Documentation Using Traceability Link Recovery, ICSA 2023, doi:10.1109/ICSA56044.2023.00021 (same author group's own prior, already-implemented TLR-based inconsistency-detection tool 'ArDoCo', which Sec.3.3 states this paper's consistency-checking mechanism directly 'adapts and extends'); the RAG-QA layer (Sec.3.5) is likewise adapted from the same group's HubLink (Kaplan, Keim, Schneider, Reussner, RAGE-KG 2025) -- this is lineage within one research group's own prior publications, not an independent confirmation from a separate tradition.
evidence_locator: Abstract and Sec.1 Introduction (p.1, problem statement and pipeline overview, Fig.1); Sec.2 State-of-the-Art (p.2, subsections 2.1-2.5, TLR/consistency/KB/LLM/QA related-work survey); Sec.3 Planned Steps (pp.3-4, subsections 3.1-3.5, extraction framework/schema/consistency/agent monitoring/QA); Sec.4 Challenges (pp.4-5, nine named open challenges including 'Temporal validity and system evolution'); References [19],[21],[23],[27] (p.5-6, HubLink, Keim et al. 2023 ArDoCo paper, Keim et al. 2025 tech report this vision extends, and Kruchten 2004).
verbatim_notes: Sec.1, p.1: 'We envision an automated pipeline that systematically extracts architectural knowledge from diverse artifacts, links them, identifies and resolves inconsistencies, and consolidates this knowledge into a structured knowledge base.' Sec.3.3, p.3: 'Keim et al. [21] demonstrated the use of traceability links for inconsistency detection, which we will adapt and extend for our multi-artifact context.' citation: Zheng, L., Shi, X., Mao, Z., Zhou, S., An, S., Hou, X., Li, J.: LineageRAG: Harnessing GraphRAG by Constructing Evidence Lineages with Source Grounding. arXiv preprint, submitted 17 Aug 2026. XiaoLab, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications / Xi'an Jiaotong University.
problem_addressed: Existing GraphRAG methods for multi-hop question answering retrieve evidence over a structured corpus graph but leave the connection between why a passage was retrieved (which sub-fact it was meant to establish) and the final answer implicit, so the evidence set can be incomplete (a multi-hop question is only partially covered) without the system detecting it. The paper adds an explicit, trackable link from each query-derived 'Evidence Demand' through graph retrieval to a verbatim source span.
state_model: An Evidence Demand rj = (idj, delta_j, Ij, Oj) is the closest unit to a state object: a query-specific sub-requirement with a fixed identifier, a natural-language description of the fact to establish, and symbolic input/output variable slots -- entirely query-scoped and discarded after the query completes. No ontological/epistemic/lifecycle classification triple; no persistent knowledge state exists between queries.
transition_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no typed S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 transition semantics and no append-only history of any kind. Every Evidence Demand, candidate pool and annotation set is constructed fresh per query (Sec.3 Problem Formulation) and nothing persists once Oq=(Sk,Wq) is returned.
provenance_model: The paper's single strongest point of overlap: each retrieved candidate passage d carries a formal provenance record Aq(d) = {(idj, l) | d = dj,l} -- the demand id and rank of every retrieval event that exposed it (Eq.5) -- and a final grounded annotation w=(iw,dw,sw,aw) is only accepted if 'provenance continuity' holds: there must exist l such that (iw,l) is in Aq(dw) (Eq.9, Sec.4 'Lineage Completion with Source Grounding'). This is a real, formally specified, empirically load-bearing provenance-gates-admission mechanism -- but it carries only demand-id and rank, not D-System's actor/authority/evidence/method/lineage tuple, and it is not a persistent record: it exists only for the query's duration.
actor_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- fully automated single-agent pipeline (one inference-time LLM performs demand induction, retrieval-guided selection, and grounding); no human role, no multi-agent structure, no authority-weighted actors. Notably even the QA reader and both judging models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini for span-support audits, Sec.5) are LLMs -- less human-in-the-loop than D-System's explicit human-agent collaborative framing, not more.
temporal_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no temporal or bitemporal model; the corpus graph G is static per experiment (built once offline, Table 8) and each query's lineage state is fully transient with no versioning concept.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no conflicting-claim arbitration or trust weighting between sources; selection favors 'complementary' (non-redundant) passages across demands (Set-Wise Selection Prompt, Sec.4), which is a coverage-maximization objective, not a conflict-resolution one. Same-title redundancy gq(d) (Eq.6) is tracked and used only for deduplication.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no independence-aware corroboration mechanism; repeated exposure nq(d) (Eq.6, count of retrieval events surfacing a candidate) is tracked as a selector feature but the paper never frames it as strengthening epistemic weight through independent paths, nor discounts derivative agreement -- it is a redundancy signal, not a convergence-scoring one.
memory_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as a persistent memory model -- the OpenIE-built corpus graph G (passage/entity nodes, extracted-relation and entity-similarity edges; built once via Qwen3-32B, Sec.5 Implementation details) functions as a fixed retrieval substrate directly reused from HippoRAG 2, not an evolving memory store; no write-back of query results into G.
retrieval_context_model: The paper's second-strongest overlap area, corresponding to D-System's H5: the query is decomposed into ordered Evidence Demands (Eq.2-3), each demand independently retrieves over the corpus graph via Personalized PageRank (Eq.4), and demand-conditioned provenance guides set-wise selection to jointly cover complementary requirements rather than redundant ones (Sec.4 'Set-wise selection'). This is demand/topology-aware context construction, empirically shown (Table 5) to matter: shuffling correct provenance across passages while preserving its volume drops R@5 by 8.11 points, worse than removing provenance entirely (-2.95) -- direct evidence that which-requirement-does-this-serve information, not just its presence, drives retrieval quality. Scoped to one QA turn; not a lineage/authority/dissent/convergence-aware context package spanning a persistent knowledge graph.
decision_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no decision object of any kind; the pipeline answers a question, it does not represent or record choices.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- Evidence Demands (Sec.4) require *established facts*, not software requirements; the vocabulary overlap ('demand', 'requirement' used informally in Sec.2 'explicit information requirements') is not a mechanism overlap with requirement derivation from decisions.
planning_model: Partial and narrow: Evidence-Demand Induction (Sec.4) decomposes a query into an ordered sequence of sub-goals whose 'joint resolution makes the answer derivable' (induction prompt, Sec.4) -- a query-decomposition plan, not a development/execution plan; no phase/task/dependency structure.
execution_unit_session_model: NOT_APPLICABLE -- one query is the unit of work; no session or execution-unit concept beyond a single inference call sequence.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no code or artifact concept; passages are natural-language corpus text (Wikipedia-derived QA benchmark passages), not source code or build artifacts.
test_verification_linkage: Partial: each candidate annotation w is checked against a formal Valid_q(w) predicate (Eq.9) requiring (a) the span is a verbatim substring of the selected source passage after normalization, (b) a schema check on the typed relation aw, and (c) provenance continuity to the demand that motivated retrieval -- a real, mechanical verification gate, but it verifies text-span grounding, not code against acceptance criteria/tests.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no deployment concept.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; the corpus is fixed benchmark text, not a running system generating telemetry.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- the corpus graph G and Evidence-Demand induction prompt are both fixed; no mechanism updates the knowledge base or the extraction process based on outcomes across queries (each query is independent, Sec.3).
forward_traceability: Partial and query-scoped: idj (the demand identifier) is carried unchanged from induction (Eq.2-3) through retrieval (Eq.4-6) through selection (Eq.7) to the final grounded annotation w=(iw,...) (Eq.8-9) -- an explicit, auditable forward chain from question-derived sub-goal to answer-supporting evidence, matching D-System's forward-traceability *pattern* but confined to one inference call rather than idea-to-runtime.
backward_traceability: The paper's clearest, empirically audited overlap with H9's backward direction: Table 6 measures, for 1,000 queries, whether each Evidence Demand's answer traces back to 'a verbatim span in the selected source' (1,865/2,182 demands grounded), and Table 6's second half has human-adjacent (GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini) judges independently verify whether 420/500 audited grounded spans fully support their linked demand -- i.e., the paper does not just claim backward traceability, it quantifies its own success rate and error modes (10/500 'wrong-demand links'). This is a rigorous, audited instance of answer-to-evidence backward tracing, though scoped to text-QA rather than functionality-to-decision tracing.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no change-impact or blast-radius mechanism; the corpus and demands are static per query, nothing is revised or propagated.
human_agent_scope: NOT_APPLICABLE (no human role) -- fully automated: one LLM performs demand induction, retrieval, selection and grounding, and two further LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini) serve as the evaluation judges (Sec.5 Metrics); D-System's human-agent collaborative framing (H6) has no analog here at all.
implementation_availability: Research-paper implementation with full experimental detail (models, prompts referenced as being in 'supplementary material', reader/retriever configuration, Table 8 cost accounting) but no GitHub or code-release link appears anywhere in the 8 pages read; whether the implementation is or will be open-sourced is NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS from the paper text alone.
evaluation_method: Rigorous quantitative benchmarking: three multi-hop QA datasets (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, 1,000 queries each) against ten baselines spanning LLM-retrieval, conventional RAG, four GraphRAG systems and three evidence-selection systems, measured by R@5/EM/F1 (Table 1); a three-way component ablation (Table 2); two further mechanism-attribution studies isolating evidence-set-construction gains (Table 3) and demand-passage-provenance correctness via a provenance-shuffling control (Table 5); a dedicated Source-Grounding audit with independent LLM-judge cross-validation (Table 6, 96.2% GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini agreement); and a token-cost accounting (Table 8). This is the most rigorously evaluated source in this dispatch's batch.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: A formally specified, empirically validated provenance-gates-admission mechanism: a grounded claim is only accepted if it carries a continuous provenance trail back to the specific requirement that motivated its retrieval (Eq.9's provenance-continuity condition), and Table 5's controlled ablation shows that scrambling correct provenance (while preserving its volume) is measurably worse than having no provenance at all (-8.11 vs -2.95 R@5 points) -- i.e., wrong provenance actively misdirects the system, not merely fails to help. This is direct, quantified, adjacent-field empirical support for the general claim underlying D-System's H3/H5 that provenance-correctness (not just provenance-presence) materially affects which information a system trusts and retrieves.
strongest_difference: No persistence: state, provenance and 'lineage' all exist only for the duration of one query and are discarded afterward -- there is no append-only history, no actor/authority model, no multi-source conflict arbitration, no temporal versioning, and no human role of any kind. The mechanism never touches decisions, requirements, specifications, plans, execution, code artifacts, tests, deployment, or runtime telemetry -- its entire scope is: decompose a question, retrieve graph passages per sub-question, and ground the answer in verbatim quotes. 'Lineage' here names a within-inference provenance trace, not a cross-time knowledge-transition history, despite the shared vocabulary with D-System's own 'lineage' language.
derivative_ancestor: Cui, Y., Widom, J., Wiener, J.L.: Tracing the Lineage of View Data in a Warehousing Environment, ACM Transactions on Database Systems 25(2), 2000, doi:10.1145/357775.357777 (explicitly named in Sec.1 as the direct conceptual source of 'evidence lineage': 'Data lineage applies the same principle to derived records by identifying the source items that produced them'); Kretzschmar, K., Watt, F.M.: Lineage Tracing, Cell 148(1-2), 2012 (biological lineage-tracing metaphor, cited alongside); Gutierrez et al. 2024 HippoRAG (NeurIPS) and Gutierrez et al. 2025 HippoRAG 2 (ICML) -- the graph index and PPR retrieval substrate LineageRAG reuses directly per its own Implementation Details (Sec.5).

R@5 falls to 68.42, which is 8.11 points below correct provenance and 5.16 points below removing it.'

source_type: preprint (self-published systems/architecture paper by an industry practitioner -- not peer-reviewed, no venue given; the author explicitly self-labels it 'a systems paper; its contributions are architectural, not empirical claims about task performance', Sec.1)
problem_addressed: Conventional agent frameworks build outward from the LLM conversation loop, adding tools/rules/logging as afterthoughts, so an agent's true state (objective, rules, tool-call record, reasoning trace, outputs) is scattered across a prompt, code, a framework's internal state, a transcript, and a lossy similarity-indexed 'memory' store -- making it hard to explain, reproduce, or safely branch what an agent did. The paper proposes ActiveGraph, a runtime where the append-only event log is the sole source of truth and the working graph is a deterministic, replayable projection (fold) of that log, with all coordination happening through reactive behaviors that read/write the shared graph.
state_model: No ontological+epistemic+lifecycle (O,E,L) classification triple and none is proposed -- ActiveGraph's typed objects (company, document, question, claim, evidence, contradiction, risk, memo in the worked 'diligence' pack) are domain-specific per pluggable 'pack', not classified along D-System's orthogonal axes. The closer match is structural: graph state is 'a typed set of objects and relations' (Sec.3) that is 'never mutated directly' but computed by folding the event log forward -- state as a derived, not primary, artifact, which is directionally the same commitment D-System's own state model makes relative to its transition log.
transition_model: Close structural match, though narrower in typing than H2 proposes: 'the append-only event log is the source of truth; the working graph is a deterministic projection of that log' (Abstract), computed by a 'replay' operation guaranteed deterministic (Sec.3). Every event carries id, type, payload, actor, an optional caused_by pointer to the triggering event, and a timestamp (Sec.3) -- functionally S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 with T=event type and P=(actor, caused_by). Two replays of the same log are proven to produce 'deterministically identical state' (Sec.3), and a 'strict replay' mode mechanically verifies reproducibility by comparing live vs. recorded event streams (Sec.4). This is event sourcing (a named, established data-systems pattern per the paper's own Sec.8) applied to agent state -- the paper explicitly frames its contribution as recombination, not invention, of the transition mechanism.
provenance_model: Partial and load-bearing: every object in the graph carries a 'provenance' block naming the creating behavior and the causing event ('nothing is created without a traceable origin', Listing 1 caption, p.5); every event carries an 'actor' field (observed values: 'runtime', 'user', or a named behavior, e.g. 'diligence.company_planner') and a caused_by pointer chaining it to its trigger. This covers actor-identity and method/mechanism provenance concretely and demonstrably, but there is no authority/domain-weighting field, no evidence-strength field, and no delegation concept -- D-System's full actor+authority+evidence+method+lineage provenance tuple (H3) is only partially present (actor + lineage + implicit method, missing authority and evidence-as-a-first-class-provenance-input).
actor_model: Single-actor-stream oriented: the observed actor values in the worked example are 'user' (who creates the initial goal) and 'runtime'/named-behaviors (autonomous). No multi-human, multi-stakeholder, or authority-weighted actor model is described; behaviors are LLM-backed routines, plain functions, classes, or relation-behaviors (logic on typed edges), not differentiated by authority or role beyond their names.
temporal_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as a bitemporal/versioning model in D-System's sense -- there is a real ordering axis (the append-only log's monotonic event sequence, replayable to any point) but no valid-time-vs-transaction-time distinction and no explicit temporal-scope field on objects; 'time' in Fig.1 is simply log-append order.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS as a designed arbitration mechanism -- the worked diligence-pack example reports the run 'detects contradictions' and produced '1 contradiction' among its 93 objects (Sec.6), showing contradiction *detection* exists as a pack-level behavior, but the paper does not describe (or the 11-page architecture text does not reach) how a detected contradiction is weighted, resolved, or arbitrated between conflicting claims; that logic would live in the open-source 'diligence' pack's behavior code, not in this architecture paper.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no independence-aware corroboration mechanism is described; multiple evidence items can 'support' a claim via typed relations (Listing/Fig.1's supports edge) but nothing in the read text discounts derivative agreement or weights independent paths differently from dependent ones.
memory_model: The paper takes an explicit, argued position against layered agent-memory systems as a category: Sec.8 states memory-layer systems (MemGPT/Letta, Zep/Graphiti, Mem0, and -- 'closest to our stance' -- Hindsight) 'share a stance: memory is derived state -- summaries, extractions, embeddings -- layered onto an agent whose primary representation lives elsewhere, and the provenance of what ends up in context is at best partial. ActiveGraph takes the opposite stance: the log is primary and everything else -- including any memory view -- is a projection of it, so provenance is total and replay is exact.' This is a direct, named critique of the exact literature D-System's own H5/memory-model claims sit adjacent to, arguing the same general direction D-System argues (memory as derived, not primary), independently and concurrently.
retrieval_context_model: Reactive, topology-based, not similarity-based: 'behaviors subscribe to patterns over events and graph shape' (Sec.1) expressed in 'a Cypher subset' (Sec.3) -- e.g. a behavior can fire on 'a claim that addresses an unanswered question' (Sec.2), a predicate over graph topology a flat event stream or a vector index cannot express. This is a genuine instance of topology-aware context/coordination (D-System's H5 claim), though scoped to triggering agent behaviors rather than to constructing a context package of state+lineage+evidence+dissent+authority+convergence for a human or agent to read.
decision_representation: Not first-class as 'decision' by name, but structurally close: 'claim' objects (a D-System System-A vocabulary term verbatim, per two_system_architecture.md's own primitive list) carry typed relations 'addresses' (to a question), 'supports' (from evidence) and 'derived_from' (to a document) (Fig.1, Sec.6) -- the worked example's central claim 'Northwind Q3 revenue grew 28% YoY to $42M' (Sec.6) is a structured, provenance-bearing, evidence-linked assertion functionally close to a D-System claim/decision node, though the paper's own vocabulary calls it a 'claim', not a 'decision', and there is no alternatives-considered or status field.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no requirement concept; the closest analog, a 'question' object generated by a question-generator behavior, is an information-gathering goal, not a requirement derived from a decision.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no specification concept.
planning_model: Partial: a 'company_planner' behavior exists in the worked pack and 'plans' in the loose sense of generating the next research questions to pursue, but there is no explicit plan/phase/task artifact with dependencies or acceptance criteria -- coordination is described as fully emergent ('no top-level script sequencing the steps of a run... The control flow is an emergent consequence of which events match which subscriptions', Sec.3), the opposite of D-System's explicit phase-as-context-boundary proposal (H8).
execution_unit_session_model: Partial: the 'frame' primitive (Sec.5) -- 'a lighter-weight in-run primitive... for parallel sub-contexts that converge back within a single run and share that run's log' -- and the fork primitive (which 'branches a run at a chosen event' into an independently-progressing log, Sec.5) are both bounded execution-unit concepts with their own budget (caps on events, behavior calls, model calls, recursion depth, wall-clock time and cost, Sec.9), functionally closer to D-System's phase/session boundary than anything else in the paper, though framed as a runtime/computational primitive rather than a planned, human-authored unit of development work.
artifact_code_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no source-code or build-artifact concept; the worked example's produced artifacts are domain objects (claims, evidence records) and a synthesized memo, not code.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE in the software-verification sense -- 'strict' replay mode is a verification mechanism, but it verifies that a run's log is byte-reproducible against itself (a determinism/replay-correctness check), not that an artifact satisfies acceptance criteria or a test suite.
deployment_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no deployment concept; ActiveGraph is a runtime library, and the worked example runs entirely offline against recorded fixtures.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed; no production-runtime telemetry or observability concept beyond the log the runtime itself produces.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: Sec.7's central architectural claim, explicitly caveated as unevaluated: because 'rules and behaviors are part of the logged state, a self-modification is itself an event', yielding two affordances -- 'auditability and rollback' (replay to before a self-modification, then strict-replay to see exactly how behavior diverged after it) and 'fork-and-diff as an evaluation primitive' (propose a change, fork at the point of proposal, run forward, structurally diff against the parent) -- 'the architecture thus supplies the cheap, honest counterfactual comparison that any credible self-improvement procedure requires. Turning these affordances into a working self-improving system is future work.' This is architecturally close to D-System's knowledge-update-closes-the-loop ambition (H11's spirit, applied reflexively to the agent's own operating rules rather than to external runtime telemetry), explicitly proposed and explicitly not yet built or evaluated.
forward_traceability: Demonstrated concretely in the worked example: an event's provenance chain (actor + caused_by + the specific llm.requested/llm.responded events, Listing 2) lets any downstream object be traced forward from the goal event that ultimately produced it, and 'replay' mechanically reconstructs this whole forward chain from the log alone (Sec.6: 'the entire causal chain from goal to memo is recoverable from the event log').
backward_traceability: The paper's most concretely demonstrated overlap with H9: 'Lineage is the deliverable... A claim object such as "Northwind Q3 revenue grew 28% YoY to $42M" carries a provenance block naming the behavior that created it (document_researcher), the event that caused it, and the specific model request event that produced it. It is linked by typed relations to the question it addresses, the document it is derived_from, and the evidence that supports it.' (Sec.6, p.9) -- a working, worked-example-verified instance of functionality/output tracing back to the specific reasoning/evidence/model-call chain that produced it, matching H9's backward direction concretely, though for an agent-output memo rather than software functionality.
change_impact_mechanism: Adjacent but distinct from H10: forking at any event and computing a 'structural diff' between the parent and the fork (Sec.5) answers 'what would have happened if I had done X differently' as a counterfactual re-run-and-compare, not as automated propagation identifying which existing downstream decisions/requirements/artifacts/tests require reassessment given an already-made change. No blast-radius or dependency-graph traversal is described; the mechanism is comparative replay, not impact propagation.
human_agent_scope: Narrower than D-System's collaborative framing: the worked example has exactly one human touchpoint (the user sets the initial goal, evt_002) after which the run is fully autonomous (103 model calls, 48 tool calls, zero orchestration code, Sec.6); no multi-agent or ongoing human-in-the-loop interaction is modeled within a run, though forking is framed (Sec.7) as the mechanism by which a human would evaluate and accept/reject a proposed self-modification.
implementation_availability: Real, working, open-source implementation (Apache-2.0 license, github.com/yoheinakajima/activegraph, pip-installable as 'activegraph'), with a fully reproducible bundled worked example ('activegraph quickstart') that runs offline against recorded fixtures in under 30 seconds and was independently re-run by the author to confirm byte-identical output counts (671 events, 93 objects, 76 relations, 103 model calls, 48 tool calls, Sec.6) -- substantially stronger implementation_availability than most sources in this campaign; unusually, this is a running, installable system rather than a described-but-unreleased prototype.
evaluation_method: Explicitly not a benchmark or empirical-performance study: 'We report no large-scale empirical evaluation of task performance; this is a systems and architecture contribution, and the quantitative artifacts we present (event counts, provenance chains, deterministic replay) are demonstrations of the mechanism rather than a benchmark study' (Sec.9). Evaluation, such as it is, consists of the worked diligence-pack example's reproducibility (identical output across re-runs) and the architecture's own determinism-contract/strict-replay mechanism functioning as a self-check.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: An event-sourced, append-only log as the sole source of truth with graph state as a deterministic, replayable projection/fold of it -- directly matching D-System's H2 transition-semantics claim at the mechanism level, not just the vocabulary level -- combined with a total, demonstrated, worked-example-verified provenance/lineage chain from goal to individual model call (H9's backward direction) using D-System's own System-A vocabulary (claim, evidence, question -- verbatim matches to two_system_architecture.md's primitive list) linked by typed relations (supports, addresses, derived_from). This is a running, open-source, independently-conceived (2026, industry practitioner, no visible awareness of D-System) system built from exactly the mechanism D-System's H2/H3/H9 claims as potentially distinctive, explicitly self-described by its own author as 'recombination' of established patterns (event sourcing, CQRS, reactive dataflow, Blackboard-era shared-state coordination) rather than a novel primitive.
strongest_difference: No orthogonal ontological+epistemic+lifecycle state classification (H1 absent); no authority-weighted or trust-arbitrated multi-actor provenance (H3 incomplete: actor+lineage present, authority+evidence-as-provenance-input absent); no independence-aware convergence/corroboration scoring (H4 absent); no explicit phase/plan/requirement/specification objects or a development lifecycle at all (System B/IES has essentially no analog -- the worked domain is investment diligence, not software development, and the substrate, while domain-agnostic in principle, is not shown applied to code/tests/deployment/runtime telemetry); no bitemporal/versioned time model (only log-order sequencing); explicitly and repeatedly self-described as an architecture/systems contribution with 'no large-scale empirical evaluation of task performance' and as a 'recombination' of pre-existing data-systems and 1980s coordination-architecture ideas rather than a new primitive.
derivative_ancestor: Two named ancestors, both in the paper's own Sec.8: (1) Nii, H.P.: The Blackboard Model of Problem Solving and the Evolution of Blackboard Architectures, AI Magazine 7(2), 1986, doi:10.1609/aimag.v7i2.537 -- the shared-knowledge-structure, react-and-write-back coordination model with no direct inter-component calls, which the paper states is 'structurally close to behaviors reacting to a shared graph', explicitly framing ActiveGraph as 'less a new idea than a vindication of an old one' for coordination; (2) Nakajima, Y.: BabyAGI, 2023, github.com/yoheinakajima/babyagi -- the same author's own prior while-loop-over-a-global-task-list agent, of which the paper states 'ActiveGraph is a direct architectural successor'. Event sourcing and CQRS (unattributed to a single citation, named as 'established patterns in data systems', Sec.2) are the third, structurally load-bearing borrowed tradition.
evidence_locator: Abstract and Sec.1 Introduction (p.1, motivation and central inversion); Sec.2 Motivation (pp.2-3, 'built around the model versus built on the log', borrowed-ideas admission); Fig.1 (p.3, full architecture diagram: graph/behaviors/event-log/operations cycle); Sec.3 Architecture (pp.3-5, replay-as-fold, Listing 1 real event trace with provenance blocks, behaviors, relation-behaviors); Sec.4 Replay and determinism (pp.6-7, determinism contract, content-addressed cache, Listing 2 real llm.requested event, strict vs. permissive replay); Sec.5 Forking and structural diff (p.8, fork mechanics, frame vs. fork); Sec.6 Worked example (pp.8-9, diligence pack, 671-event/93-object/76-relation run, lineage-is-the-deliverable claim); Sec.7 Self-improving agents affordance (p.9, explicitly caveated as unevaluated); Sec.8 Related work (pp.9-10, memory-layer systems critique, event sourcing/CQRS, Blackboard architectures, BabyAGI lineage); Sec.9 Limitations and conclusion (pp.10-11, failure modes, explicit no-empirical-evaluation statement); References (p.11).
verbatim_notes: Abstract: 'The append-only event log is the source of truth; the working graph is a deterministic projection of that log.' Sec.6, p.9: 'Lineage is the deliverable. The point of the example is not the memo; it is that every statement in the memo is traceable... this recoverable chain from goal to output, reconstructable from the log alone, is the actual product.' Sec.8, p.9-10: 'ActiveGraph takes the opposite stance: the log is primary and everything else -- including any memory view -- is a projection of it, so provenance is total and replay is exact.' Sec.9, p.10: 'We report no large-scale empirical evaluation of task performance; this is a systems and architecture contribution.'

citation: Procko, T.: On the Provenance of Software Systems: Automating Software Traceability with Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model Synergy. PhD dissertation, Electrical Engineering & Computer Science, Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, defended Spring 2025. Chair/Advisor: Omar Ochoa; committee: Massood Towhidnejad, Nicholas Del Rio, Alex Vargas, Keith Garfield.
source_type: tech report (doctoral dissertation; the contract's source_type enum has no dissertation bucket, so 'tech report' is used, matching this same dispatch's de-boer-architectural-knowledge-management-dissertation-2009 convention from X1)
problem_addressed: Development activities (a developer's decisions, rationale, and process steps) leave little to no automatic, structured trace; existing provenance is either absent or manually documented, so downstream stakeholders cannot reliably ask 'what happened, why, and by whom' about a project artifact. The dissertation's ProvTracer system aims to automatically generate and maintain a 'machine-readable, human-interpretable, extensible provenance record' for every development artifact by passively observing a developer's work session and using a multimodal LLM to infer structured provenance from that observation.
state_model: Grounded in the W3C PROV-O ontology (Entity/Activity/Agent classes and their generation/usage/derivation relations) combined with the Basic Formal Ontology (BFO) for upper-level categorization -- per the ERAU abstract and the GitHub repository's own ontology file (provtracer-o.ttl, described as maintaining 'semantic interoperability with established standards'). This is a more formally ontology-grounded state model than most sources in this campaign, though built on a pre-existing standard rather than D-System's own proposed orthogonal ontological+epistemic+lifecycle triple; NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS whether the dissertation's own schema chapters extend PROV-O/BFO with additional D-System-relevant axes, since those chapters were not reachable.
transition_model: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS as a formally presented mechanism -- PROV-O's own Activity/generation/derivation relations are inherently transition-like (an Activity connects a prior Entity state to a resulting one), and the GitHub README describes 'chained sub-graphs representing individual timeslices, which aggregate into comprehensive provenance traces', which is suggestive of an append-only, time-ordered transition structure -- but whether the dissertation formalizes this as a typed S_t--[T,P]-->S_t+1 transition scheme (versus simply tagging entities with standard PROV-O relations) could not be confirmed from the abstract and repository README alone.
provenance_model: The dissertation's central subject and this source's strongest overlap area: every artifact is to carry an automatically-generated, PROV-O-grounded provenance record built from multimodal capture (screenshots, keyboard/mouse/window/clipboard events per the GitHub README) processed by GPT-4o-family models into 'traceable links between development activities and resulting artifacts' (ERAU abstract). This matches D-System's H3 ambition at the level of intent (provenance-bearing links from activity to artifact) but the actual provenance content is activity/agent/timestamp per PROV-O's standard schema, not D-System's full actor+authority+evidence+method+lineage tuple; NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS whether authority or evidence-weighting fields are added.
actor_model: Single-developer, session-scoped: capture is of one developer's own screen, keyboard, mouse, window and clipboard activity during a bounded 'work session' (Open-Ended or Side-by-Side mode, GitHub README); the LLM functions as a passive observer/inference agent (PROV-O Agent role), not an active collaborator or a second stakeholder. NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS whether the dissertation's evaluation or later chapters extend this to multi-developer or multi-agent scope; the abstract mentions no such extension.
temporal_model: Partial and concrete: the GitHub README states the system produces 'chained sub-graphs representing individual timeslices, which aggregate into comprehensive provenance traces' -- an explicit, time-ordered chunking of the captured session -- but whether this constitutes a bitemporal (valid-time vs. transaction-time) model or simple sequential timestamping is NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS without the dissertation's schema chapters.
conflict_trust_mechanism: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- neither the abstract nor the GitHub README mentions conflicting-claim arbitration or trust weighting; the single-developer-session scope gives no structural indication that multiple, potentially-conflicting provenance sources are ever reconciled.
convergence_independence_mechanism: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- not mentioned in either source read; no independence-aware corroboration concept is described.
memory_model: The accumulating provenance knowledge graph itself is the memory artifact: stored per work-session in timestamped output folders (GitHub README), intended per the ERAU abstract to let developers/stakeholders later 'understand, query, maintain, integrate, and trust the evolution of their projects and systems' -- project/team memory of process and rationale, not an agent's own conversational or episodic memory.
retrieval_context_model: Dual and concrete: SPARQL for 'quantitative analysis' and LLM-based natural-language querying for 'qualitative insights' over the same provenance graph (GitHub README) -- a real, working instance of structured-graph-plus-NL-query context retrieval, matching D-System's H5 ambition at the mechanism level, though scoped to one developer's own captured session data rather than a topology-aware, multi-source, lineage/dissent/authority-weighted context package.
decision_representation: Named as a target capability -- the abstract states the system aims to 'extract developer rationale' -- but NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS whether rationale/decisions become a first-class typed graph object (a PROV-O Entity/Activity subclass with its own schema) or remain unstructured GPT-generated text attached to a captured event; the dissertation's schema chapters, which would settle this, were not reachable.
requirement_derivation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- no requirement concept appears in the abstract or the GitHub README; the system's scope is activity-to-artifact provenance capture, not requirements derived from decisions.
specification_representation: NOT_APPLICABLE -- not addressed in the abstract or README; no specification concept.
planning_model: NOT_APPLICABLE as a planning object -- 'Side-by-Side Mode' is described as a capture-mode setting for 'structured development tasks' (GitHub README), not a plan/phase/task artifact with dependencies or acceptance criteria.
execution_unit_session_model: Real and concrete: a bounded 'work session' (Open-Ended or Side-by-Side mode) is the system's explicit unit of capture, each producing its own session folder of chained timeslice sub-graphs -- structurally close to D-System's H8 phase-as-context-boundary proposal, though the boundary is defined by when the developer starts/stops the capture tool rather than by a planned, acceptance-criteria-bound unit of development work.
artifact_code_linkage: Central and directly claimed: 'traceable links between development activities and resulting artifacts' (ERAU abstract) is the dissertation's stated core deliverable, and the GitHub README frames the target artifacts as including 'AI/ML output provenance' specifically ('reproducibility auditing and lineage tracing in defense AI pipelines') -- suggesting the artifact scope leans toward ML-pipeline outputs and code together rather than source code alone; NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS for the precise artifact taxonomy without the dissertation's own chapters.
test_verification_linkage: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- neither source read mentions test suites, acceptance criteria, or a verification-linkage mechanism.
deployment_linkage: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- neither source read mentions deployment.
runtime_observation_linkage: NOT_APPLICABLE as D-System's H11 production-runtime-to-knowledge loop -- the system's 'observation' is development-time workstation activity capture (screenshots, peripheral input), not a deployed system's production runtime telemetry or incidents; this is development-process observation, a different stage than D-System's runtime-observation concept.
feedback_to_knowledge_mechanism: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- neither source read describes a mechanism by which captured provenance revises or updates the knowledge base's own extraction rules or schema over time.
forward_traceability: Claimed directly as a target capability: 'automatically generate and maintain project life cycle provenance' (ERAU abstract) implies a development-activity-to-artifact forward chain, and PROV-O's own generation/derivation relations are inherently forward-traceable; NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS for mechanism detail or a worked example, since the dissertation's own presentation was not reachable.
backward_traceability: Also claimed directly: artifacts are to carry provenance records that let a reader trace back to the 'implicit processes' (developer activity, rationale) that produced them (ERAU abstract: 'bridges implicit processes and explicit traces') -- matching D-System's H9 backward direction in stated purpose; NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS for mechanism detail or a worked/evaluated example, unlike log-is-the-agent-event-sourced-reactive-graphs-2026 (this same dispatch, source 3) which demonstrates its equivalent claim with a concrete worked trace.
change_impact_mechanism: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- the abstract's 'support project management activities' is the closest hint but specifies no blast-radius or dependency-propagation mechanism; not addressed in the GitHub README either.
human_agent_scope: Human-agent collaborative but asymmetric and single-human: the developer works normally while an LLM (GPT-4o/4o-mini/4-turbo) passively observes screen and input activity and infers structured provenance without active developer participation in the capture step -- a distinctive 'ambient/implicit observation' pattern (agent as silent inferencer rather than active collaborator), contemporary (2025) and relevant to D-System's H6 framing though scoped to one developer rather than a multi-stakeholder team.
implementation_availability: Real, working, open-source prototype: github.com/PR0CK0/ProvTracer, a documented PyQt6 desktop application (screenshot/input capture at 1-10s intervals, GPT-4o-family processing, provtracer-o.ttl PROV-O+BFO ontology file, SPARQL and LLM query interfaces, two capture modes) -- among the stronger implementation_availability entries in this batch, comparable to this same dispatch's log-is-the-agent-event-sourced-reactive-graphs-2026 (ActiveGraph) in being a running, installable system rather than a described-but-unreleased prototype.
evaluation_method: NOT_DETERMINABLE_FROM_ACCESS -- neither the ERAU abstract nor the GitHub README describes an evaluation methodology (user study, benchmark comparison, or case study); this is dissertation-chapter content that the Cloudflare-blocked full text would be needed to assess.
strongest_dsystem_overlap: An automated, ambient (screenshot/input-event-driven, GPT-inferred) capture pipeline producing a standards-grounded (PROV-O+BFO) provenance knowledge graph explicitly aimed at 'traceability,' 'explainability,' 'reproducibility,' and extracting 'developer rationale' for project-management use -- a working, concurrently-developed (2025) system converging on the same target as D-System's H7/H9: an automatically-maintained, artifact-linked provenance graph spanning development activity. The capture mechanism (passive workstation observation via screenshots and peripheral-device events) differs sharply in kind from D-System's structured event/decision recording, but the destination data model (PROV-O Entity/Activity/Agent triples with generation/derivation relations) and the stated goals (bidirectional traceability, rationale extraction, reduced information overload) are a genuine, independently-arrived-at convergence on the same problem framing.
strongest_difference: Capture is single-developer and ambient/passive rather than structured/explicit; no visible multi-actor authority/conflict/convergence model; no requirement/specification/plan/test/deployment objects are named anywhere in the accessible material, and the system's own framing leans toward ML-pipeline reproducibility auditing ('defense AI pipelines') rather than general software knowledge management.
